facts.value: Graduates of an accredited biomedical science degree programme can apply for the NHS' Scientist training programme, which gives successful applicants an opportunity to work in a clinical setting whilst also studying towards an MSc or Doctoral qualification.

Graduates commonly proceed to advanced degrees (M.Sc. or Ph.D.) in biomedical and life sciences, join research laboratories in universities, hospitals, biotechnology firms, or pharmaceutical companies, or use the degree as preparation for professional studies such as medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, or public health.
Many graduates work in the pharmaceutical and drug-development industry, contributing to preclinical research, diagnostic development, and translational projects.
Pharmacist, Biomedical Scientist, Biomedical Engineer, Lab Manager, Research Associate
research and laboratory work aiming for the improvement and advancement of medical knowledge
finding new medicines to fight cancer, 3D printing a heart, growing embryos for IVF

Students learn how to gather information from various sources to make well-informed decisions regarding biological matters. They learn how to design and carry out scientific experiments, and they also discuss ethical concerns such as responsible research techniques.
